name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,330

clue.text: Nicer pulp read? Strange line (13)

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder are made strange, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a pulp novel is a nicer read, then finds a line of it strange.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'read' splits the clue in two: the first part is only fodder, and 'line' at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A perpendicular is a line drawn at right angles to another.

clue.text: Pray and give offerings, daily almost, at the outset — here? (6)

definitions.text: Pray and give offerings, daily almost, at the outset — here?

indicators.note: take each word's letter at its outset, its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: Pray and give offerings, daily almost
blocks.note: first letters of Pray, And, Give, Offerings, Daily, Almost

explanation.surface: A worshipper is told to pray and bring offerings nearly every day, and asks where.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: read as a sentence, it describes what people do at a pagoda, and 'here?' points to the place.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered temple in East Asia where people pray and leave offerings.

clue.text: Say again, referring to contents of cited charge (9)

indicators.note: the contents of a word are its inside letters, without the ends

blocks.note: re = referring to, as in a memo heading
cITEd without its first and last letters
a rate is a charge, as in an hourly rate

explanation.surface: A lawyer repeats the wording of the charge cited against a client.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contents of' means strip the first and last letters, leaving only the inside of 'cited'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: repeating a statement is saying it over again.

clue.text: Some marvel, eg antique, stylish (7)

indicators.note: only some of the letters in the following words are used

explanation.surface: A collector admires a stylish marvel, an antique piece for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma and 'eg' make the surface look like a list, which disguises the join where the answer spans three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe refined, graceful taste.

clue.text: Flier’s parent, not short on stages of journey (5,8)

blocks.note: legs are the stages of a journey

explanation.surface: A pilot's father never skimps on the length of any leg of the trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot, and 'Flier’s parent' seems to belong together; in fact the definition stops at 'Flier' and ’s means 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A daddy longlegs, the crane fly, is a long-legged flying insect.

clue.text: Constant abuse? This might bring luck, some say (5)

definitions.text: This might bring luck, some say

blocks.note: c is the constant for the speed of light
to abuse something is to harm it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether putting up with constant abuse could somehow be lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constant abuse' reads as one phrase, but it splits into two pieces; 'some say' belongs to the definition, since a lucky charm only brings luck by belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm, such as a lucky charm, is an object thought to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Slippery type coming up? Shelter! (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word coming up is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A warning cry: a slippery character is approaching, so take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Shelter!' a cry to take cover; it is the definition, and the slippery type written upwards fills the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind.

clue.text: Note theatrical act’s second coming (6)

blocks.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a turn is a performer's act on stage

explanation.surface: A critic notes that a stage act is about to be repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second coming' sounds religious, but here it only means coming back again.
explanation.definitionFit: A return is a coming back, a second arrival at the same place.

clue.text: Good story about Democrat’s move without hesitations (5)

indicators.note: the story goes around the D, placed about it

blocks.note: a lie is a made-up story
first letter of Democrat, placed inside LIE

explanation.surface: A flattering account of a politician's smooth, confident manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good story' reads as praise for a tale, but it splits: G, then a story that wraps round the D.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide is to move smoothly and continuously, without stops or hesitations.

clue.text: Laid back English Conservative, first to try Scouse? (7)

indicators.note: the word is read back to front
take the first letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: LAID is taken as it stands

explanation.surface: A relaxed English Tory is the first to sample something from Liverpool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' seems to mean relaxed, but it splits into LAID and a reversal instruction. Scouse is the dialect of Liverpool, and the question mark flags that it is an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is a dialect: the speech of Liverpool, in the north-west of England.

clue.text: Journal including expert’s case in relation to eating (7)

indicators.note: the diary includes the other letters inside it
a word's case is its outer shell, the first and last letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of ExperT, placed inside DIARY

explanation.surface: A journal reports an expert's case study on nutrition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' here means the outside of a word, its first and last letters, so the expert contributes only two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary means relating to diet, to what one eats.

clue.text: House way of behaving, they say (5)

indicators.note: what people say is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: a manner is a way of behaving; the word is heard, and its sound matches a house

explanation.surface: A remark about the way a household conducts itself.
explanation.walkthrough: MANNER and MANOR sound the same in most accents; the spelling of the house is what goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A manor is a large country house with its lands.

clue.text: Greek character, neat, overseeing part of hospital food (9)

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece overseeing another sits above it

blocks.note: nu is the Greek letter N
ENT = the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A tidy Greek figure supervises the catering in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT, the ear, nose and throat department, is the usual 'part of hospital'; 'overseeing' puts the other pieces above it in a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: nourishment, whatever feeds a body.

clue.text: Spaceman, second from earth, travelling to Saturn (9)

indicators.note: take the second letter from the word
the letters travel, moving into a new order

explanation.surface: A space traveller is the second to leave Earth on a voyage to Saturn.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a spaceman's voyage, and it hides that 'to' belongs to the fodder rather than giving the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut is a person who travels into space.

clue.text: One checking car on hill (7)

blocks.note: Audi is a make of car
a tor is a rocky hill, placed after AUDI

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a car parked on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, a word common on Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is one who checks accounts.

clue.text: Piece of music used by person at assembly (6)

indicators.note: the answer is held in the words and used by them

explanation.surface: A piece of music is played by someone at a school assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used by' tells you the answer is carried inside the next words, running across the word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical composition, often for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Information on the German grammatical category (6)

blocks.note: der is German for 'the', placed after GEN

explanation.surface: Notes on how German grammar sorts its nouns.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: German gender, with der, die and das, is a famous hurdle for learners.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is a grammatical category, such as masculine or feminine.

clue.text: Finished before time — obvious (5)

indicators.note: one piece comes before the other

explanation.surface: Something that ended ahead of schedule, as was plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finished before time' reads as ending early; it is two pieces in order, with T the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and obvious, not hidden.

clue.text: Publicity material linked to film that is in metal case (3,2)

indicators.note: the IE goes in the metal case

blocks.note: a tin is a metal case, holding IE

explanation.surface: Promotional goods for a movie, with the film reel kept in a metal canister.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on to 'film', where it seems to end at 'material'; 'that is in metal case' sounds like the old film can, and is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a product or promotion linked to a film or show.

clue.text: Divine dog — lie back ultimately relaxed? (7)

indicators.note: take the ultimate, last letter of the word
the letters are loosened and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A heavenly dog lies back and takes it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie back' looks like a reversal, and reversing DOG to GOD is tempting; but 'back' is only there to give its last letter K, and the anagram does the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Godlike means like a god, divine.

clue.text: Late, the confused competitor (7)

indicators.note: the letters are confused, mixed up

explanation.surface: A competitor turns up late and bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'Late' tempts a reading about a dead competitor; 'the' is fodder too, not a filler.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: athletes are the people who compete in races and field events.

clue.text: Border somehow brought up, in part (3)

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing letters up reads them bottom to top
only part of the word is used

explanation.surface: Someone's upbringing was only partly a matter of borders, one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The border is buried backwards in the third word: its middle letters, read upwards, give the edge of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A hem is the folded border of a piece of cloth.

clue.text: Overly sentimental director’s original material (5)

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A mawkish film director's first script turns out soppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original material' reads as a script or screenplay; the definition is only 'material', meaning cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth.

clue.text: Manager modified arms tradition (13)

indicators.note: the letters are modified into a new order

explanation.surface: A manager changes a long-standing military custom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms tradition' reads as a military custom; every letter of both words is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrator is someone who manages an organisation.
